segments.text: Hello and welcome to National Reporter.
I'm Madhav Das Kupala.
For days now, the National Capital has been witnessing a political showdown.
And at the center of it is one man, Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
This week, opposition leaders led by Rahul Gandhi took to the streets of Delhi.
staging a dharna and demanding his resignation.
The protests were followed by a series of detentions.
The opposition alleges that the special intensive revision of voter lists is tilting the playing field in BJP's favour.
The election commission, however, has repeatedly dismissed these charges as baseless.
But what triggered this political flashpoint?
It was a newspaper report that in fact talked about how a new declaration on Form 6 was introduced despite objections coming in from two election commissioners.
The report also raised questions over alleged arbitrary decisions by CEC Yanish Kumar.
Now despite the dissent coming in from the two other commissioners who later went on to write letters to the cabinet secretary as well.
And now this controversy has reached the Supreme Court.
With the top court issuing notice to the election commission seeking its response to the allegations, the political showdown at the national capital continues.
Let's quickly take you through the first set of talking points that we have as far as today's debate is concerned.
The first demand is that CEC Gyanesh Kumar must resign.
This is what opposition says.
The second is that they should act against the CEC over the Form 6 change.
Third, reverse the new declaration in Form 6.
Number four, scrap the SIR of voter lists taking place across India.
End police action on opposition protesters and also CEC Gyanesh must meet opposition members of parliament.
Now these are the demands coming in from the opposition political parties, but what is the
political face-off all about.
On the one hand, you have Rahul Gandhi who says that we wrote to the Election Commission for a meeting.
Election Commission says they didn't get any letter from the opposition.
Later, of course, they say that the CEC is not meeting us.
Opposition says it's an unusual request to meet 240 MPs.
Also, say that the meeting must be held at Parliament annexed.
And EC says protocol bars meets outside of the Election Commission of India.
Now, this is as far as a face-off between the two are concerned.
Election Commission also saying they tried to send a representative, but that didn't quite work out.
There are several unanswered questions that still remain.
Some of them the Election Commission has addressed, but what remains unanswered?
One, why has EC not addressed issues via a press conference and put out all the facts?
Where are the dissent notes that are reportedly being fired by election commissioners in relation to the important decisions?
Is the declaration attached to Form 6
lawful or has it happened in an unlawful manner as the opposition insists?
Is the Supreme Court order upholding forms of exchange applicable to the declaration specifically?
That's something that perhaps the courts will have to adjudicate on.
Is the announcement of special camps an admission of discrepancies that the existing process has?
Why did the election commissioners not make reservations on ECI net and send that letter directly to the president?
These are some of the questions that still remain.
Let me introduce our panelists joining us here in the studio.
With us is Charu Pragya, spokesperson of BJP.
Subrash Taz, founder of The Churn.
With us is Shashank Shekhar Jha, lawyer of Supreme Court.
Shivam Bhagat, the spokesperson of the Congress Party.
Vaibhav Srivastava, spokesperson of the Aam Aadmi Party.
And Dharmendra Yadav, spokesperson of Samajwadi Party.
Meher Pasri Jha, spokesperson of the CJP, also joins us over here.
Shivam Bhagat, question that is coming in from the BJP is that if you have evidence of violation in the SIR process, take that evidence, approach the Supreme Court and take the legal route.
Why are you protesting on the streets of the national capital is the question coming in from the BJP.
Your response?

We are protesting on the streets of the national capital because in the last 10 months, 14 instances of dissent have been proved and have come out in the public that two election commissioners had dissented against the CEC.
When the election commissioners themselves are dissenting, then why cannot the citizens and the opposition ask questions of this government?
Is this a democracy anymore?
The founding fathers of our country had created the post of the election commissioner and had created the election commissioner to uphold the constitution.
But today, under the leadership of
the CEC, Mr. Gyanesh Kumar, it has become a tool for vote-chori, a tool for disenfranchising millions of legit voters.
Now the proof is in the pudding.
Why was, multiple points, why was Form 6 messed around with?
The Supreme Court has come down heavily on them on the Form 6 issue.
Justice Bhuvan of the Supreme Court, and let me quote you what he said, which is a very big deal.
Justice Bhuin's quote, you can dig out that quote, but let me get a response from Charu Pragya on that.
The basic problem is voter disenfranchisement.
That is completely unacceptable.
And this is destruction of democracy as we know it, is what opposition is saying.
And that's why opposition is coming together.
Most opposition parties at least are on the streets protesting on this issue.
And they're protesting as we speak.
Madaf, good evening and namaste to everyone.
I want to break down this into two different parts.
The issue which is in the court regarding the SIR, regarding the election commission and what is happening on the streets of Delhi today also while we speak.
And these are distinct issues Madaf because as you know right now there is a hearing which is underway in the courts.
You know what happened at this hearing today?
What happened at this hearing today is that the organizers of the protest decided not to even turn up.
It's not even important to turn up for a judicial hearing which would have made whatever it is that you're doing on the streets of Delhi somewhat legitimate.
Instead what is happening?
Instead what is happening is, this is headline grabbing, this is opposition leaders trying to get their 15 seconds of fame.
This is opposition leaders trying to bring in so much of dramatics into an issue that should have remained judicial with evidence.
That has stopped existing.
If Shivam wants to quote one chief justice to me or one judge to me, I want to quote the letter which was written yesterday by 42 former judges of the high courts and supreme courts.
They have very clearly said that contest an election.
Do not delegitimize an election.
They have requested the media that your headline is not evidence.
Evidence is what is put in court.
And what did the court decide?
When the petitioners went to court, their demand was simple.
The CEC should be removed.
Did the courts do that?
No.

No, I am going to quote your mother.
